contentBlocks.text: If a recipe calls for 2 cups of flour for every 3 cups of sugar, that's a ratio — a comparison between two quantities. This week, you'll learn to work with ratios like a mathematician.

A ratio compares two quantities, and can be written three ways: 'the ratio of flour to sugar is 2 to 3,' '2:3,' or as a fraction '2/3.' Order matters — the ratio of flour to sugar (2:3) is different from the ratio of sugar to flour (3:2). Look at a group of objects around you (like a set of pencils and pens, or red and blue items) and write the ratio comparing the two groups, in all three forms.
You just described a real comparison using ratio language in three different forms. Tomorrow we'll learn how to find equivalent ratios that describe the same comparison at a different scale.

objectives: Define a ratio as a comparison between two quantities
Write a ratio in three forms: 'a to b,' 'a:b,' and 'a/b'
materialsNeeded: A group of two different countable objects (pencils/pens, red/blue items)
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Introduce the recipe example and the three ways to write a ratio.
2. Emphasize that order matters — flour:sugar is different from sugar:flour.
3. Have the child count real objects and write the ratio in all three forms.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's topic: equivalent ratios.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just the ':' notation before introducing the fraction and 'to' forms
Ready for more: ask them to find a ratio in their own life (like a sports team's win-loss record) and describe it in all three forms
The order-matters point is genuinely easy to overlook — spend real time on it with concrete, countable examples
teacherGuide.answerKey: Answers will vary based on the child's chosen objects — check that the ratio is written correctly in all three forms and that the order matches what was actually asked for.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 6 Ratios & Proportional Relationships standard 6.RP.1: understanding the concept of a ratio and using ratio language.

generationData.instructions: Write each ratio in the requested form.

rows.problem: A bowl has 5 apples and 3 oranges. Write the ratio of apples to oranges using ':' notation.
Write the same ratio (apples to oranges) using 'to' notation.
Write the ratio of oranges to apples using ':' notation.
